claims.text: Selective laser melting can tune the magnetocaloric behavior of non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
SLM can engineer grain size, defect density, and nanoscale precipitates in non-equiatomic HEAs.
Changes in grain size, defect density, and nanoscale precipitates alter magnetic exchange interactions and magnetic ordering temperatures.
A conventionally cast or equilibrated non-equiatomic HEA has a random distribution of constituent elements.
Controlled SLM processing produces a non-equilibrium microstructure through rapid solidification.
Varying laser power, scan speed, and hatch spacing induces changes in defect density, grain size, and secondary-phase precipitation.
The proposed measurements would be conducted on thin films or microfabricated specimens.
SLM processing can produce high dislocation density in an HEA.
SLM processing produces refined grains and nanoscale precipitates in the target non-equiatomic HEAs.
Nanoscale precipitates created by SLM act as pinning centers.
SLM-induced microstructural changes tailor the local environment in which magnetic atoms interact.
Controlled lattice defects and altered phase distributions can shift the magnetic ordering temperature.
Controlled lattice defects and altered phase distributions can enhance or diminish the magnetocaloric effect.
Compared with conventionally processed alloys, SLM-processed non-equiatomic HEAs will exhibit a shifted magnetic ordering temperature.
Compared with conventionally processed alloys, SLM-processed non-equiatomic HEAs will exhibit a measurable change in magnetocaloric-effect magnitude.
The direction of the magnetocaloric change depends on how the modified microstructure alters magnetic exchange interactions.
The hypothesis applies only when processing-induced microstructural changes are large enough to influence magnetic exchange interactions.
Alloy composition and specimen dimensions may delimit the applicable processing window.
SLM strongly affects the microstructure and mechanical properties of an equiatomic HEA.
The direct impact of SLM on magnetocaloric properties in non-equiatomic HEAs remains unquantified and requires experimental verification.
